- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 5.0), model often overcorrects with exaggerated downward swings; cap subsequent forecast drops at 30% of peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price history shows mean reversion, model tends to overpredict; apply 15–25% downward adjustment for 14–30d horizon.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates; add 5–15% to forecast for 1–14d horizon.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (first 5–7 days), model often fails to capture it; apply 20–40% downward bias to first 5 days of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (negative sentiment), model tends to underforecast; add 10–20% to forecast for 1–7d horizon.
- When sentiment is high and price is stable, model often overestimates; apply 10–20% downward adjustment for 14–30d horizon.
- If model forecast exceeds true outcome by >2.0 in any 7-day window, reduce forecast by 15–30% for next 7d horizon unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
